                    ### Question
                    Which of the following semi-solid pharmaceutical forms with which a master formula can be prepared has greater occlusivity ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Hydrophobic ointments
opb. Hydrophobic or water-oily creams.
opc. Hydrophilic or ole-aqueous creams.
opd. Hydrophilic ointments

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In evaluating the occlusivity of semi-solid pharmaceutical forms, hydrophobic ointments are known to have the greatest occlusivity due to their high lipid content, which forms a barrier on the skin and effectively prevents water loss. This aligns with the consensus that lipid-rich formulations provide superior occlusivity. Hydrophobic or water-oily creams have moderate occlusivity because they contain a moderate amount of lipids, allowing for some barrier formation and partial water loss prevention. Hydrophilic or ole-aqueous creams, with low lipid content, offer minimal occlusivity as they form a limited barrier. Hydrophilic ointments, being water-based, do not form a barrier and thus provide minimal occlusivity. The retrieved evidence path regarding lipids and skin physiology supports the understanding that lipid content is crucial for occlusivity, confirming the consensus that hydrophobic ointments are the most occlusive option.
